evidence: engine/transport/factory_owner_root.go:209 -- root := &FactoryOwnerRoot{binding: binding, acquiredCtx: ctx, rootSHA: rootSHA, capture: capture, limits: map[string]FactoryOwnerComponent{}, counts: map[string]int{}, components: map[string]string{}}
Synthetic isolated Linux overlay scope-deadline-probe.log: physical admission accepted after verified scope expiry and after verified route expiry while outer context remained live.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject ACKs already past scope or route expiry and clamp the acquired context to the earliest authenticated expiry and outer deadline. Independently bind the separate Root lease deadline; it is not in the v2 ACK. Add discriminating late-ACK and later-call tests.
findings.title: Enforce authenticated scope and route expiration during owner authority
findings.why_it_matters: The v2 ACK validates the scope but the acquired authority remains bound only to the outer context. After the wallet begin succeeds, an ACK or later physical operation can cross scope or route expiry while outer authority remains live. Both expiration paths were reproduced through in-memory BeginFactoryPhysical in a synthetic Linux overlay.
findings.validation_reason: The saved v2 source creates acquiredCtx from the outer context at factory_owner_root.go:209, stores the verified scope without clamping at :238-247, and checks only acquiredCtx.Err at :252; factory_owner_scope_v2.go:51-55,183-187 validates timestamp ordering and digest but not current time, while harness_spending.rs:535-539 checks liveness at begin only and gateway_transport.py:173-176 derives the outer deadline independently of scope/route expiry, so a later authorized physical call can cross either bound when the outer context survives; this source-level precondition is reachable but production incidence was not measured and the reported remote synthetic log was not independently inspected.
